overview: Markets: Wall Street and Sensex/Nifty both rose as falling oil prices lifted sentiment on Iran diplomacy hopes.
Big story: Iran offered a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to shipping.

items.headline: Iran offers seven-day plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz to US
items.summary: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran has proposed a seven-day timeline to reopen Hormuz to shipping, conditional on the US lifting its naval blockade, releasing at least $12bn in frozen assets and easing oil sanctions. The White House has not confirmed acceptance, but a deal would ease record fuel prices and cut inflation risk for oil-importing economies like India.

items.headline: US to detail Trump-Xi trade truce terms Monday, tariff exemptions expected
items.summary: USTR Jamieson Greer said full details of the US-China trade agreement, including product exemptions and an extension of the tariff truce to January 10, will be released Monday. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the truce will hold after Xi's first US state visit in 11 years, a key signal for global supply chains and markets watching for a fresh escalation.

items.headline: ArcelorMittal halts Ukraine's biggest steel plant after Russian strikes
items.summary: ArcelorMittal will not resume operations at its Kryvyi Rih plant, Ukraine's largest steelworks, after four Russian missile strikes in five weeks killed five workers and injured 17. The company expects a roughly $1 billion non-cash impairment charge, underscoring how deep Russian strikes on industrial infrastructure are hitting Ukraine's economy and Western investment there.

items.headline: Netanyahu calls Gaza genocide claims 'biggest lie' in UN speech
items.summary: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu told the UN General Assembly that genocide allegations over Gaza were the 'biggest lie of the century,' as scores of delegates walked out, whom he branded 'moral cowards.' The speech deepened Israel's diplomatic isolation even as ceasefire violations continue on the ground in Gaza.

items.headline: UN Security Council condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
items.summary: The UN Security Council condemned escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi civilian and energy infrastructure, as Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani military chiefs prepared to meet on supporting Riyadh under a joint defence pact. The move signals growing international alarm over a widening Gulf security crisis tied to the broader regional war.

items.headline: Ukrainian drones hit Russian oil refinery and rail targets overnight
items.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes forced Russia's Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery to suspend operations and hit a passenger train and other targets, while Russian strikes killed civilians in Perm and Belgorod regions. The tit-for-tat strikes on energy infrastructure highlight how both sides are targeting fuel supply as a war-fighting lever ahead of winter.

items.headline: Pakistan strikes Afghan targets after deadly Kohat mosque bombing
items.summary: Pakistan carried out air and drone strikes on Taliban positions across four Afghan provinces after drones from Afghanistan were downed near the border, following a September 18 mosque bombing in Kohat that killed at least 31 people. The escalation marks a sharp deterioration in Pakistan-Afghanistan relations with regional security implications.

items.headline: Nepal PM tells UN climate crisis punishes low-emission nations
items.summary: Nepali PM Balendra Shah told the UN General Assembly that Nepal's recent deadly floods show climate change hurts countries that barely contributed to it, noting Nepal emits less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gases. The remarks add pressure on rich nations ahead of upcoming climate-finance negotiations.

items.headline: Fitch, S&P, OECD and ADB raise India's FY27 growth forecast to 6.9-7.1%
items.summary: Multiple global agencies upgraded India's growth outlook for the coming fiscal year to between 6.9% and 7.1%, citing resilient domestic demand and easing inflation. The upgrades reinforce India's position as the fastest-growing major economy, a key data point for consulting and policy interviews on India's macro trajectory.

items.headline: SEBI cuts PMS minimum investment threshold from Rs 50 lakh to Rs 25 lakh
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India introduced a new Portfolio Management Services framework, halving the minimum investment threshold and allowing PMS managers to invest directly in mutual funds, ETFs and specialised investment funds. The reform widens access to professionally managed portfolios and is part of SEBI's push to deepen capital markets.

items.headline: States told to notify four labour codes by October 31
items.summary: The central government asked all states and union territories to publish implementation rules for India's four consolidated labour codes, covering wages, industrial relations, social security and occupational safety, by October 31. The codes are a major overhaul of India's labour law framework with significant implications for hiring, gig work and compliance costs.

items.headline: Supreme Court dismisses plea to make Hindi the official court language
items.summary: The Supreme Court rejected a petition seeking Hindi as the official language of courts, saying language reforms are already being introduced in phases. Separately, the Court split on whether to refer a challenge to the Election Commission Act to a larger bench, while backing a permanent five-judge constitutional bench.

items.headline: Supreme Court acquits rape accused, cites flawed witness-testimony approach
items.summary: The Supreme Court acquitted a man convicted of rape, ruling that a court cannot accept part of a witness's testimony while rejecting the rest without clear justification. The judgment reinforces evidentiary standards in sexual-assault trials and is likely to be cited in future criminal appeals.

items.headline: Sensex gains 300 points, Nifty tops 23,100 as oil prices ease
items.summary: The Sensex rose 300.90 points (0.41%) to 73,881.44 and the Nifty50 gained 65 points (0.28%) to 23,128.10, with auto and realty stocks leading gains. Falling crude prices on hopes of an Iran diplomatic breakthrough supported sentiment despite elevated US bond yields.

items.headline: Wall Street ends volatile week higher; S&P 500 up 0.51%
items.summary: The S&P 500 climbed 0.51% to 7,743.41, the Dow rose 0.93% to 51,828.62, and the Nasdaq gained 0.5% to 27,068.72, as easing oil prices offset a surge in Treasury yields. The rebound came amid optimism over the Trump-Xi trade truce and hopes for an Iran diplomatic breakthrough.

items.headline: Spacetech startup Pixxel raises $100 million Series C
items.summary: Bengaluru-based space technology startup Pixxel raised $100 million from Temasek and Seraphim Space, the largest funding round yet for an Indian spacetech company, taking its total funding to $195 million. The deal capped a week in which Indian startups raised over $412 million, up 42% week-on-week.

items.headline: AceVector (Snapdeal) launches IPO with Rs 30-32 price band
items.summary: AceVector, formerly Snapdeal, opened a mainboard IPO comprising a Rs 287 crore fresh issue and Rs 133 crore offer-for-sale at a Rs 30-32 price band, part of a wider 'IPO rush' of Indian companies racing to list before SEBI's extended approvals lapse. Four IPOs together aim to raise about Rs 1,776 crore this week.

items.headline: FIIs sell Rs 5,027 crore of Indian equities as DIIs keep buying
items.summary: Foreign institutional investors sold Rs 5,027.36 crore of Indian shares while domestic institutional investors bought Rs 4,301.18 crore, continuing a pattern of foreign outflows being cushioned by domestic buying. The divergence highlights how domestic mutual funds and insurers are increasingly setting the floor for Indian markets.

items.headline: Google launches Gemini 3.8 Live with real-time avatar video
items.summary: Google released Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar in Gemini Enterprise, combining live dialogue with near-real-time video generation that keeps facial expressions and lip-sync accurate across 97 languages. The launch pushes Google further into real-time multimodal AI, a race also involving OpenAI and Meta.

items.headline: Sanders and Casar introduce bill to ban superintelligent AI
items.summary: Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, which would prohibit AI systems exceeding human cognitive performance, pause advanced AI development pending federal safety rules, and create a cabinet-level Department of Artificial Intelligence. Violators could face criminal penalties, reflecting growing US political anxiety over frontier AI.

items.headline: Alibaba cuts Qwen audio API prices by up to 95%
items.summary: Alibaba's Qwen team released a new voice stack, Qwen-Audio 3.1, alongside price cuts of up to 95% on its audio APIs. The move intensifies price competition among Chinese AI labs racing to win developer adoption for voice and multimodal applications globally.

items.headline: Ando raises $20 million to build AI-native team chat app
items.summary: Startup Ando came out of stealth with a team messaging app designed to let AI agents participate as first-class members of conversations, backed by a $20 million pre-seed and seed raise. It reflects a wider bet that workplace chat tools will be rebuilt around AI agents rather than just humans.

items.headline: India's kabaddi teams chase Asian Games gold against Iran
items.summary: Both Indian kabaddi teams face Iran in Asian Games gold-medal matches in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with the men chasing a ninth title and the women a fourth. PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen also opened their badminton singles campaigns the same day after the shock men's doubles exit of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty.

items.headline: West Indies begin India tour with first Test from September 27
items.summary: The West Indies cricket team arrives in India for a multi-format tour beginning September 27, its first assignment of the 2026-27 international season. The series gives India a chance to test bench strength ahead of a packed home season.

items.headline: Laver Cup and F1 Baku Grand Prix both open in same weekend
items.summary: The Laver Cup tennis exhibition began in London while Formula 1's Baku Grand Prix weekend continued in Azerbaijan, giving fans a packed international sports weekend. Both events draw global broadcast and sponsorship interest, illustrating sport's growing overlap with entertainment marketing.
